Bridgit listens on the phone for the words you choose. Only what you say after one goes to its control agent; nothing before it is kept or sent. Android\'s green microphone dot shows while it listens.
%1$d of %2$d. Each one goes to the control agent you pick.

Wake words need an offline English speech model on the phone: Vosk small English (US) 0.15, made by Alpha Cephei (free, Apache 2.0). Tap Download and wait for it to finish (about a minute on Wi‑Fi), then add your wake words below. It comes once from alphacephei.com and is checked with SHA-256 before use. After that, listening works offline and audio never leaves the phone.
%1$s, %2$s on this phone. Works offline; from alphacephei.com (Apache 2.0), checked with SHA-256.

Lets your control agents take a screenshot when they ask

Bridgit uses this only to take a screenshot when one of your control agents asks, and only while Screenshots is on in Bridgit\'s Features. It can\'t read, tap or type on your screen. Every screenshot shows a notification and is logged. Apps that block screenshots come out blank.

Read battery (level, charging, health, temperature, battery saver), network, screen and sound context. Control agents hear when the battery runs low.

Let control agents with Agent Super Powers change Bridgit\'s settings and the phone\'s sound and display. Control agents can never turn this off or on, stop the listener, or change their own permissions.
Change DND, sound, brightness, screen timeout and battery saver. Timed changes can be undone.
Turn on the torch for up to ten minutes.
Ring and vibrate for up to one minute, respecting sound settings.
Read light, pressure, proximity, motion, orientation and steps where supported.
Files stay in app storage for 30 days. Review, export or delete in Files and Android access.
Choose a control agent when sharing text, links or files from Android.
Select individual files in Files and Android access; control agents cannot browse your Downloads folder.
Control agents with Agent Super Powers can run shell commands: tap, type, open apps, change settings. Set up in More → ADB setup.
Every request needs your Copy tap in Files and Android access; expires after five minutes.
Read foreground-time summaries after granting Usage access.
Sensitive notification text may be exposed. Requires notification access; kept only in memory.
Read only steps, sleep and heart rate you explicitly grant. No health writes.
Record front or rear camera video for 1–30 seconds. Optional audio needs microphone access.
Read accessible videos or a still frame; Android selection permissions apply.
Find things in a photo (the dog, each dirty dish, faces) and zoom in on them. Faces are found on the phone; anything else is sent to a cheap cloud vision model.
Recognize Latin-script text locally in an image. No cloud recognition.
Approve screen access once, for one hour or sixteen hours. Android can stop it sooner; each grant belongs to one control agent.

Private control agent control reads visible app content and performs actions you approve. Use only your own control agents. Password fields and system permission controls are excluded. Stop at any time. This is not an accessibility tool.

Your answer reached %1$s. Closing in 5 seconds.
Connect devices on the same Wi-Fi. Choose Add to applets to control which applets can use each device. Camera video stays on your network; applets may send photos to their selected models.
Enter the camera’s local IP address and camera account. Enable local access in the camera’s own app first. Available controls depend on the camera.
In Tapo, open Device Settings → Advanced Settings → Camera Account. Create a separate camera username and password, then enter them here. Keep the camera on the same Wi-Fi.

Snapshots and small pan / tilt commands for cameras you add locally. Separate control agent permission; no phone camera permission needed.

Bridgit takes a fresh photo from the selected local camera every 10 seconds and asks your chosen models when the scene changes. The tablet screen can be off. Keep Bridgit running on the same Wi-Fi with internet access for the AI checks. The latest photo stays in memory; Pet monitor history keeps the readings.
Devices map: this phone in the middle and the devices around it
Inspect applets, required models, device membership and sharing status. Changes need a separate configuration grant and your approval on the phone.
Let granted control agents find services and IP addresses on this device’s direct Wi-Fi or Ethernet network. Partial inventory only.
Let granted control agents verify and save supported local devices with credentials you authorize. Each enrollment belongs to that control agent.
Let granted control agents read their enrolled routers and devices, and switch supported Shelly Gen1 relays. Camera capture keeps its separate permission.
Let granted control agents read and change which enrolled external devices each applet may use. Enrollment alone never adds a device to an applet.
Let granted control agents explicitly record 1–30 second sound clips from enrolled camera microphones. Separate from phone microphone and camera photo access.
Let granted control agents send bounded audio clips to supported enrolled camera speakers. Separate permission; no automatic playback during enrollment.

Aim this camera at the food bowls first. Save its current pan/tilt position and enable its microphone for five-second samples, once every sampling interval (default 20 seconds). Audio goes to Clef to estimate eating/drinking sounds. A confident sound will turn this camera to the saved view and take photos for 30 seconds. Photos confirm activity; sound cannot identify your pet or confirm a meal. Brief sounds may be missed.

Let authorized control agents connect to your computers and servers, run commands, manage files and schedule tasks. Uses saved credentials and verified host keys. Shell access has the remote account’s full permissions.
Link a spare Bridgit phone to this one. The phone you add is a satellite: your control agents can use its camera, microphone, speaker and more through this phone, the hub.
Off pauses it: the satellite can\'t show this %1$s\'s Home, use its applets or pause its control agents.

Each time you finish with the card, this device sends the result to your private portal at bridgit.cc: scores, moves and counts as numbers and words, never pictures. Kept 30 days. Only you, and people you invite, can see it. You can stop it here at any time.

About once a minute this device sends today\'s counts, each check\'s answer, the notices it sent and its pause state to your private portal at bridgit.cc, plus a small photo of the latest check (at most one a minute). Kept 30 days. Only you, and people you invite, can see it. You can pause it from the portal and stop it here at any time.
You use this applet in Applets › Portals.

This device copies the applet\'s rows and photos to your private portal at bridgit.cc, and you use the applet there, in Applets › Portals or on a computer. Kept until you stop the portal or remove the applet. Only you, and people you invite, can see it.
Uploads stop, viewers lose access and this applet\'s rows and photos are deleted from the server. They stay on this device.
This stops it and deletes everything it set up on this device: its watches and their counts, its schedule, its workflow, its card and its permissions.
The most this applet may spend on cloud checks, counted across all devices working for this applet. When a limit is reached, the applet pauses until the limit resets or you raise it.
